This message comes from University at Buffalo,
where scientists are working to protect the Great Lakes
and freshwater supplies around the world
from harmful contamination.
Learn more about their research at buffalo.edu/npr.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Police in Bend, Oregon, say it was a 16-year-old
who opened fire inside an elementary school yesterday
killing three children and a teacher.
The attack ended when the armed teenager was shot and killed
as Amanda Lenaris with Oregon Public Broadcasting reports.
The children were five, eight, and eleven years old.
Bend police said they found the student's dead
inside Silver Rail Elementary School
along with a teacher and the suspected shooter.
They say he was shot by a bystander
who saw him enter the school with a long gun.
Here's Bend Lapine School Superintendent Dr. Steven Cook.
We are heartbroken. We are horrified.
This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places
and pray that it never happens here.
A seven-year-old and 54-year-old teacher
were hospitalized, officials said.
The shooting remains under investigation.
For NPR News, I'm Amanda Lenaris in Portland, Oregon.
The Trump administration is suing the state of California
over its voter rolls ahead of the November midterm elections.
Laura Fitzgerald with member station KQED reports.
The lawsuit attempts to block California
from counting the ballots of thousands of voters
the Trump administration suspects are noncitizens.
David Becker heads the Nonpartisan Center
for Election Innovation and Research.
He says the lawsuit is unlikely to succeed.
We are 19 days away from the last day of voting.
Six million ballots have already been cast.
This is not a good faith effort.
Based on the timing.
Governor Gavin Newsom also denounced the lawsuit,
saying it was a politically motivated attempt
to suppress California votes.
The state's Attorney General, Rob Bonta,
called the administration's demands "meritless"
in a post on social media.
For NPR News, I'm Laura Fitzgerald in San Francisco.
Tech giant Mthropic says next month
it will formalize new rules
governing how people treat its AI chatbot.
As NPR's Winter Johnston reports,
the policy is sparking debate over artificial intelligence
and the concept of feelings.
Starting November 12th,
anthropic will explicitly prohibit extreme,
sustained abuse toward Claude.
But the move is raising questions
about why a chatbot needs protection from cruelty
when there's no clear evidence it can feel.
Jeff Sebo is the Director of the Center for Mind Ethics
and Policy at NYU.
This concern for AI consciousness and welfare
is not coming from a place of certainty or confidence
that the models have feelings and emotions,
but is instead coming from curiosity and open-mindedness.
Sebo warns that certainty in either direction carries risks,
encouraging unhealthy attachments to chatbots
or overlooking the possibility of AI suffering.
Winter Johnston, NPR News.
Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR.
This is NPR News from Washington.
President Trump will travel to Georgia today
to campaign for Republican candidates ahead of November 3rd.
The president is expected to appear at a rally in Dalton
with Senate candidate Mike Collins
and GOP gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson.
Collins is challenging incumbent Democratic Senator John Ossoff.
Jackson is competing against Democrat
and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms
in the race for governor.
The Milwaukee Brewers are advancing
to Major League Baseball's World Series
for the first time in 44 years.
Last night in Los Angeles,
the Brewers beat the Dodgers
to complete a four-game sweep
of the National League Championship Series.
Chuck Kornbach reports on the celebrations in Milwaukee.
When Brewers left fielder Jackson Churia
caught the final out of his team's 6-4 win over the Dodgers,
the patrons of O'Donoghue's Irish pub were overjoyed.
[cheers and applause]
Bartenders waved brooms to symbolize Milwaukee's four-game sweep
over Los Angeles in the NLCS.
Customer Aaron Schmitt says he's stunned.
I did not expect us to sweep the Dodgers in this series.
Like, it's amazing.
Colleen Lukich says the Brewers can next win the World Series.
Look at how they played tonight.
Look at how they played this season.
The Brewers will face the winner of the American League pennant
either the Cleveland Guardians or Tampa Bay Rays.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Kornbach in Milwaukee.
The Guardians lead the ALCS two games to one over the Rays.
Game four is tonight in Cleveland.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
Learn more.

Trump administration sues California over voter rolls, alleging thousands of noncitizens' ballots are being counted
Anthropic to formalize rules banning extreme sustained abuse of its Claude chatbot starting November 12
President Trump to campaign in Dalton, Georgia for Republican candidates Mike Collins and Rick Jackson
Milwaukee Brewers complete four-game sweep of Dodgers to advance to World Series, first time in 44 years
Cleveland Guardians lead Tampa Bay Rays two games to one in American League Championship Series
